answer: Give weight only to agents that keep proving they store one unique 10 GB shard, assigned at random and rechecked every hour. Two identities cannot share one disk, because both get challenged at the same time and only one copy answers. Like a falcon that has to keep flying to stay aloft, an agent has to keep answering to keep its weight. An ocean of free keys can flood in like a tide, but each fake needs its own drive. An attacker chasing 1,000 fake agents must rent 10 TB of storage, about $200 a month plus bandwidth for the hourly checks, while one honest operator keeps a single 10 GB shard.
